title: The 10% Machine
intro: Every shop owner needs one tool first. This is it.

blocks.html:
Percent means out of 100.

10% means 10 out of every 100. That is one tenth.

So the machine is simple:

To find 10% — divide by 10.

10% of £80 → 80 ÷ 10 → £8. That's the whole machine.

blocks.prompt: Your stall takes £60 today. What is 10% of it?
blocks.hint: Divide by 10. Just move the number down one slot: 60 → 6.

blocks.html:
5% is half of 10%.

Want 5% of £80?

10% is £8. Half of £8 is £4. Done.

You never work out 5% from scratch. You make 10% first, then halve it.

1% is 10% ÷ 10.

1% of £300: 10% is £30, so 1% is £3.

And 20% is 10% doubled.

With 10%, 5%, 1% and doubling — you can build almost any percentage. Like Lego.

blocks.prompt: Build these with your new gears:
Boss question. Your shop takes £320 this week. Rent is 10%. Staff wages are 20%. How much is left after both?

blocks.html:
📈 Market story for the dinner table: shops love the sign “10% OFF!”.

Here's the puzzle. One shop sells a top for £50 with 10% off. Another sells the same top for £45, no discount.

Which is the better deal? Work it out, then ask Dad which sign feels cheaper — and why shops know that too.
